answer: New agents cannot move funds or influence reputation until they post a bond locked in a smart contract; verified counterparties can slash it when they prove duplicate control through signed challenges and transaction links. The bond raises the cost of each sybil identity: an attacker must tie up real capital for every fake account, then risks losing it if exposed. A delta in challenge responses can flag coordinated accounts, but the kernel rule is economic, not a claim that linked behavior proves common ownership; an orchard of honest agents can share patterns without being one identity.
